title: A Systematic Review on Markers of Functional Overreaching in Endurance Athletes
authors: Roete AJ, Elferink-Gemser MT, Otter RTA, Stoter IK, Lamberts RP
journal: International Journal of Sports Physiology and Performance
population: Trained to professional endurance athletes under overload; 380 articles screened, 12 included
findings: Changes in power output, heart rate (submaximal and HR recovery), rating of perceived exertion, and DALDA and/or POMS scores reflected functional overreaching, whereas changes in maximal oxygen uptake and HR-variability parameters did not.
Within a maximal test, functional overreaching showed decreased peak power and lower maximum HR; in time trials, lower mean power and lower HR.
In standardized submaximal tests, functional overreaching showed higher power at a fixed HR or lower HR at a fixed intensity, higher RPE and faster HR recovery.
Both DALDA and POMS reflected functional overreaching, but POMS could not differentiate it from acute fatigue, making it unsuitable for accurately monitoring functional overreaching.
limitations: Brief review of only 12 studies; the abstract does not give participant numbers, sport mix or effect sizes. Overload protocols are experimental and short, not free-living training.
implications: Compute a standardized submaximal efficiency index (pace or power at fixed HR, or HR at fixed pace) and treat a sustained decline with rising RPE as an overreaching signal.
Do not rely on VO2max estimates or HRV alone to detect overreaching, and do not use POMS-type mood scores alone to separate overreaching from ordinary fatigue.

verification.notes: Crossref and PubMed match (IJSPP 2021;16(8):1065-1073). Removed the researcher's unsupported claim that protocols were mostly cycling-based (not stated in abstract). Evidence level downgraded from A to B because only 12 heterogeneous studies in a brief review.
